---
title: "Still at Home"
subtitle: "Living Arrangements of Young Adults (18–34) Across Florida"
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(leaflet)

# Read in downloaded Census data and tract boundaries
sarasota <- read_rds("sarasota.rds")
tracts <- read_rds("tracts.rds")

# 1. Number and percentage of 18-34 year olds living at home by tract
young_adults <- sarasota |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# 3. Volusia County data and tract boundaries
volusia <- read_rds("volusia.rds")
volusia_tracts <- read_rds("volusia_tracts.rds")

volusia_young_adults <- volusia |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# 4. Central Florida regional data and tract boundaries
cf_data <- read_rds("central_florida.rds")
cf_tracts <- read_rds("central_florida_tracts.rds")
cf_counties <- read_rds("central_florida_counties.rds")

cf_young_adults <- cf_data |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# 5. County comparison: Sarasota, Volusia, and Orange
county_comparison <- bind_rows(
  young_adults |>
    summarize(
      county = "Sarasota",
      total_18_34 = sum(total_18_34, na.rm = TRUE),
      living_at_home = sum(living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
  volusia_young_adults |>
    summarize(
      county = "Volusia",
      total_18_34 = sum(total_18_34, na.rm = TRUE),
      living_at_home = sum(living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
  cf_young_adults |>
    filter(str_detect(NAME, "Orange County")) |>
    summarize(
      county = "Orange",
      total_18_34 = sum(total_18_34, na.rm = TRUE),
      living_at_home = sum(living_at_home, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = 100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34))

# 6. Nationwide state-level data and boundaries
states_data <- read_rds("states_data.rds")
states_geo <- read_rds("states_geo.rds")

states_young_adults <- states_data |>
  filter(variable %in% c("B09021_008", "B09021_012")) |>
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) |>
  rename(total_18_34 = B09021_008, living_at_home = B09021_012) |>
  mutate(pct_at_home = round(100 * (living_at_home / total_18_34), 1))

states_map_sf <- states_geo |>
  left_join(states_young_adults, by = "GEOID")
```

Where do young adults in Florida live with their parents? Using data from the US Census Bureau's 2018–2022 American Community Survey (ACS), we map tract-level geographic patterns across Sarasota and Volusia Counties, zoom out to Central Florida, and compare regional drivers.

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Florida Counties

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Sarasota County

Sarasota County exhibits notable geographic variation: inland and southern tracts around North Port show higher proportions of young adults living with parents compared to coastal and downtown neighborhoods.

```{r}
#| label: plot-map
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

# Coordinates for major Sarasota County cities to provide geographic context
major_cities <- tibble(
  city = c("Sarasota", "Venice", "North Port"),
  lon = c(-82.543, -82.430, -82.198),
  lat = c(27.339, 27.100, 27.058)
)

tracts |>
  left_join(young_adults, by = "GEOID") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_at_home), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = major_cities, aes(x = lon, y = lat), color = "black", size = 2) +
  geom_label(
    data = major_cities,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 3.5,
    fill = "white",
    alpha = 0.85,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    option = "plasma",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Geographic Patterns of Young Adults Living with Parents",
    subtitle = "Percentage of adults aged 18–34 living with parents by Sarasota County tract",
    fill = "Living with\nparents",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

### Volusia County

In Volusia County, young adults living with parents are particularly concentrated in suburban inland communities like Deltona, contrasted with coastal tracts near Daytona Beach and New Smyrna Beach.

```{r}
#| label: plot-volusia-map
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

  lon = c(-81.099, -81.288, -81.214, -80.965),
  lat = c(29.198, 29.023, 28.905, 29.025)
)

volusia_tracts |>
  left_join(volusia_young_adults, by = "GEOID") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_at_home), color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = volusia_cities, aes(x = lon, y = lat), color = "black", size = 2) +
  geom_label(
    data = volusia_cities,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 3.5,
    fill = "white",
    alpha = 0.85,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
```

### Central Florida Region

Zooming out to seven counties across Central Florida (Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Lake, Brevard, Volusia, and Polk) highlights a regional divide: rates are highest across southern inland tracts, while central Orlando tracts feature lower shares.

```{r}
#| label: plot-central-florida-map
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-align: center

# Coordinates for major Central Florida anchor cities
cf_cities <- tibble(
  city = c("Orlando", "Kissimmee", "Sanford", "Daytona Beach", "Melbourne", "Lakeland"),
  lon = c(-81.337, -81.417, -81.276, -81.099, -80.663, -81.954),
  lat = c(28.477, 28.304, 28.789, 29.198, 28.109, 28.056)
)

cf_tracts |>
  left_join(cf_young_adults, by = "GEOID") |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = pct_at_home), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = cf_counties, fill = NA, color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = cf_cities, aes(x = lon, y = lat), color = "black", size = 2) +
  geom_label(
    data = cf_cities,
    aes(x = lon, y = lat, label = city),
    vjust = -0.6,
    size = 3.2,
    fill = "white",
    alpha = 0.85,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    option = "plasma",
    na.value = "grey90"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Geographic Patterns of Young Adults Living with Parents",
    subtitle = "Percentage of adults aged 18–34 living with parents across Central Florida",
    fill = "Living with\nparents",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS (Orange, Seminole, Osceola, Lake, Brevard, Volusia, Polk)"
  ) +
  theme_void()
```

### County Comparison

```{r}
#| label: plot-county-comparison
#| warning: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

county_comparison |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(county, pct_at_home, .desc = TRUE), y = pct_at_home)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1d3557", width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(pct_at_home, 1), "%")),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = scales::label_percent(scale = 1),
    limits = c(0, 50)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Percentage of Young Adults (18–34) Living with Parents",
    subtitle = "Comparing Sarasota, Volusia, and Orange Counties",
    x = "County",
    y = "Percentage living with parents",
    caption = "Source: US Census Bureau 2018–2022 ACS"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```

Among these three counties, **Sarasota** has the highest share of young adults living with parents (**36.5%**), followed by **Volusia** (**34.2%**), while **Orange County** has the lowest (**32.5%**).

Several key factors likely drive these differences:

- **College Enrollment & Student Rentals:** Orange County is home to the University of Central Florida (UCF), which enrolls over 68,000 students. Many students and recent graduates live in dense student apartments, off-campus shared housing, and dorms around eastern Orlando as roommates rather than living at home with parents.
- **Housing Costs & Retiree-Heavy Demographics:** Sarasota is an affluent coastal county with a high median age and steep housing and rental prices. For young adults entering the local workforce, high cost of living makes independent renting significantly more challenging.
- **Urban Density vs. Suburban/Coastal Communities:** Orange County's dense urban core provides a broader inventory of multi-family apartments and starter rental units compared to the single-family and retirement-oriented neighborhoods common in Sarasota and Volusia.

### Osceola County

Across all of Central Florida, **Osceola County** stands out with nearly half (**47.9%**) of young adults living with parents—the highest rate in the region. 

::: {.callout-note}
#### Key Factors Behind Osceola's High Rate
1. **Multigenerational Family Norms:** Osceola County has a majority Hispanic population (56.1%). In Hispanic cultures, multigenerational living and young adults remaining in the family home until marriage or financial stability is culturally valued and common.
2. **Tourism & Service-Sector Wages:** Much of Osceola's economy is tied to the hospitality and service industries supporting the Kissimmee and Walt Disney World corridor. Because these positions often pay entry-level wages while regional rent prices have surged, young workers are often financially priced out of independent living.
3. **Absence of a Large Residential University Influx:** Unlike Orange County, Osceola does not have a massive residential university drawing tens of thousands of independent young adult renters from outside the area.
:::

:::

## United States

How do Florida's rates compare across the rest of the United States? The interactive map below shows the percentage of young adults (18–34) living with their parents in each state. Hover over or tap any state to view its exact percentage.

```{r}
#| label: plot-interactive-states-map
#| warning: false

# Color palette matching the project plasma theme
pal <- colorNumeric("plasma", domain = states_map_sf$pct_at_home)

leaflet(states_map_sf, height = 500, width = "100%") |>
  addProviderTiles(providers$CartoDB.Positron) |>
  setView(lng = -96, lat = 37.8, zoom = 4) |>
  addPolygons(
    fillColor = ~pal(pct_at_home),
    weight = 1,
    opacity = 1,
    color = "white",
    dashArray = "3",
    fillOpacity = 0.75,
    highlightOptions = highlightOptions(
      weight = 2,
      color = "#333",
      fillOpacity = 0.9,
      bringToFront = TRUE
    ),
    label = ~paste0(NAME.x, ": ", pct_at_home, "% living with parents"),
    labelOptions = labelOptions(
      style = list("font-weight" = "normal", padding = "3px 8px"),
      textsize = "13px",
      direction = "auto"
    )
  ) |>
  addLegend(
    pal = pal,
    values = ~pct_at_home,
    opacity = 0.75,
    title = "Living with<br>Parents (%)",
    position = "bottomright"
  )
```
